lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 26, which gives every explainer a narration and renders all their videos on your machine.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
Every issue PR still starts with its explainer page, written with the explainer skill.
Now it also gets a narration: one spoken line per diagram box, step and table row.
Stamping saves the page text each line was written from, and a hash of the whole page.
Step four: the new CI step checks the branch's issue, every explainer the PR touches, and all of them when the tool changes.
On your machine, videos-all.sh fetches and keeps a gallery folder at the latest main.
lines.say: On your machine, the videos-all script fetches, and keeps a gallery folder at the latest main.

lines.caption: It collects every page from main and from the issue branches, without a checkout.
It decides by content hash: an unchanged page is skipped, and a stale narration is reported.
Then it renders what changed, and prints a report of every page.
Cloud sessions can write and check a narration, but can't make the voice. So the session writes it, and your machine renders.
A narration is tied to its page by content, never by file dates, so a stale line is found with Chrome alone.
Step two: the skill and CLAUDE.md now require the narration in every issue PR.
Step three: after any later page edit, the stale lines are rewritten and stamped again.
Step four: the new CI step checks the branch's issue and every explainer the PR touches.
Step six: a branch provides only the explainer files it changed, and two branches on one issue are a conflict.
Step eight: the script exits with an error if any render failed.
A page with no narration, or a stale one, is listed for you instead of rendered.
An unchanged page is skipped. A new or changed one is rendered.
A page changed by two branches is a conflict, and a failed render keeps its log.
Pages 1, 3 and 7 got their narrations. Page 1 first needed the ids and keys a narration points at.
The narrations of pages 9 and 11 still match their pages.
The PR changes the skill, CLAUDE.md, the explainer job and its script, and adds videos-all.sh and five narrations.
lines.say: The PR changes the skill, Claude dot M D, the explainer job and its script, and adds the videos-all script and five narrations.

lines.caption: To undo the CI check, delete its one step from the workflow.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It follows issue 25, copies the two narrations that already rendered, and joins the explainer job's pattern.
In the cloud container, full Chromium hung, so the narration tools use the headless shell.
The stamps of 9 and 11 still match, and the four new narrations passed status and render's own checks.
Page 1 renders exactly as before: not one pixel differs.
Locally, the CI step passed a current narration and failed a missing one.
On this PR's first push, before this page had a narration, CI's new step went red, as it should.
When the narration was pushed, the same step went green, with all four narrations current.
In a test repo, the script picked each page's source, reported a conflict, and ignored non-issue branches.
After the review fixes, it refused to reset anything but its own gallery, and preferred each issue's own branch.
With a stand-in for the render, it rendered, then skipped, then re-rendered only the page that changed.
After CI's review, the new paths were run too: a tool change checks every narration, and a table row re-renders every page.
A real render with Kokoro, and how it says the new lines, were not run. Kokoro is only on your machine.
A fresh local agent found eight issues, one high and four medium. Six are fixed and one is accepted.
The high one: pointed at your own checkout, the script could have thrown away uncommitted work. Now it refuses.
Merged branches no longer override main, and an issue's own branch wins over others.
CI's own review raised sixty-two findings over seven rounds. All but fourteen are fixed, and those fourteen are accepted.
Your first real run, the sound of the new lines, and the check on the next PR all come after the merge.
Part 3. What comes later: your first local run.
Run the script once, listen, fix any word, and from then on each PR arrives narrated.
Run it, then run it again: the second time, everything should be skipped.
A word Kokoro gets wrong gets a row in the pronunciation table, and the next run re-renders every page.
That's the tour: every explainer now has a narration CI checks, and one script renders them all on your machine.
